entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states includes the Republic of Indonesia for 1945 to 1949, with Jakarta as capital. The list says its independence was recognized de facto by the Netherlands, and de jure, meaning formally in law, by Egypt, Syria and Lebanon.

entries_new.name: Liberated Area of Cambodia
entries_new.founder: Kampuchean United Front for National Salvation
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Liberated Area of Cambodia as territory controlled by the Kampuchean United Front for National Salvation, with its capital in Snuol district. The list says that in 1979 Vietnam took over Phnom Penh, and the next day the Kampuchean People's Revolutionary Council Government was established to replace the Liberated Area.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Islamic Revolutionary State of Afghanistan
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Islamic Revolutionary State of Afghanistan as a small Salafist state in the northern Bashgal Valley. The list says it was founded in 1980 by the cleric Mawlawi Afzal during the Afghan mujahideen insurgency. The row gives no capital and no end date beyond that year.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Gorno-Badakhshan Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says that when civil war broke out in Tajikistan in 1992, the local government in Gorno-Badakhshan declared independence from the Republic of Tajikistan. Khorugh was its capital. The row gives no end date beyond that year.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Islamic Emirate of Badakhshan
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Islamic Emirate of Badakhshan as an unrecognized Islamic state ruled by Sharia law in what is now Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan. The list dates it to 1996 and names Badakhshan as the capital. It gives no founder or end date.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Islamic Republic of Qa'im
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says that during the 2005 occupation of Al-Qa'im by Al-Qaeda in Iraq, the group declared the Islamic Republic of Qa'im. Al-Qa'im, in present-day Iraq, was the capital. The row gives no further detail on its governance or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Islamic Emirate of Rafah
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Islamic Emirate of Rafah as a short-lived unrecognized Islamic state in Rafah. Jund Ansar Allah founded it by declaring independence in 2009, two years after the Hamas takeover of Gaza. The list says it collapsed after the 2009 Battle of Rafah.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Bangsamoro Republik
entries_new.stopped_by: Armed Forces of the Philippines, September 28, 2013
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says the Moro National Liberation Front self-declared the Bangsamoro Republic, with Davao City and Zamboanga City as its listed capitals. The list says the republic ceased to exist after the front's defeat in Zamboanga City by the Armed Forces of the Philippines on September 28, 2013.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Emirate of Azaz
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says the Emirate of Azaz was proclaimed by the Islamic State following its capture of Azaz in 2013. Azaz, in Syria, was its capital, and the list dates it 2013 to 2014. The row gives no further detail on its governance or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (2013 to 2014)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states records the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant for 2013 to 2014, with Baqubah as capital. The list says it was proclaimed after the Islamic State of Iraq expanded into Syria, and that it was later abolished and replaced with the Islamic State.

entries_new.name: Miecław's State
entries_new.stopped_by: Casimir the Restorer, duke of Poland, in 1047
entries_new.story: Miecław's State was a state in Masovia with its capital at Płock. Wikipedia's list says Miecław formed it around 1037 by breaking away from the Duchy of Poland during a crisis inside the country. It lasted until 1047, when Casimir the Restorer, duke of Poland, reconquered it into the Duchy of Poland.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Despotate of Lovech
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states dates the Despotate of Lovech 1330 to 1446, with Lovech as capital. The list says that after the core Bulgarian state fell to the Ottomans in 1396, Lovech Fortress remained unconquered for another 50 years, until after the Crusade of Varna.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Four Kingdoms of Estonia
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Four Kingdoms of Estonia as an anti-Christian state established in 1343 by pagan Estonian rebels during the Saint George's Night Uprising. It was ruled by the Four Kings of Estonia. Tallinn is given as the capital.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Saaremaa
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Kingdom of Saaremaa as an anti-Christian state established in 1344 by pagan Estonian rebels during the Saint George's Night Uprising. It was ruled by King Vesse of Saaremaa, and its capital was Pöide Castle on the island of Saaremaa.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Duchy of Gniewkowo
entries_new.story: The Duchy of Gniewkowo was a district principality and fiefdom within the Kingdom of Poland during the era of fragmentation. Wikipedia's list says it was formed in 1314 from part of the Duchy of Inowrocław, lay in Kuyavia, and consisted of the Gniewkowo and Słońsk Lands. The list dates its listed periods 1373 to 1374 and 1375 to 1377.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Croatia (interregnum of 1526 to 1527)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says that after the heirless Jagiellonian king Louis II died on 29 August 1526, Croatia was left kingless until the 1527 election at Cetin. There the Sabor, the Croatian assembly, elected the Habsburg Archduke Ferdinand of Austria as king on 1 January 1527. Six Croatian nobles and four representatives of the Archduke sealed the charter.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Tsardom of Bačka
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says that after the Hungarian kingdom fell at the Battle of Mohács, Tsar Jovan Nenad established a short-lived Serbian rump state in Vojvodina, with Subotica as capital. The list dates it 1526 to 1527 and says it later fell at the Battle of Sződfalva.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom
entries_new.challenge: Habsburg claim to all of Hungary
entries_new.recognition: Ottoman backing, per the list
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom as ruled by the Ottoman-backed Zápolya dynasty, which did not accept the Habsburg claim over the whole of Hungary. It lists the periods 1526 to 1551 and 1556 to 1570, and capitals at Buda, Lipova and Alba Iulia. The area is now split among Slovakia, Hungary, Romania and Ukraine.
entries_new.anchor: Buda, Lipova and Alba Iulia (Hungary, Romania)

entries_new.name: Duchy of Syrmia
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says Duke Radoslav Čelnik, who had served in Jovan Nenad's army, moved power from Bačka to Syrmia after the tsar's death. He ruled the region for three to five years, until the Ottomans conquered it. Slankamen was the capital, and the list dates the duchy 1527 to 1530 or 1532.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Polish-Swedish union
entries_new.story: The Polish-Swedish union was declared by Polish king Sigismund III Vasa, who also succeeded his father, the Swedish king John III Vasa. Wikipedia's list says it led to a Swedish civil war that ended with Sigismund being ejected from Sweden and the union dissolving. Polish kings kept an uninterrupted claim on the Swedish throne until 1660.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Bohemia (1618 to 1620)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says that at the start of the Thirty Years' War the Bohemian kingdom declared independence from the Habsburg monarchy and temporarily elected Frederick V of the Palatinate as its new king. The list says the rebels were defeated at the Battle of the White Mountain. Prague was the capital.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Catalan Republic (1640 to 1641)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says the Catalan Republic was declared during the Reapers' War. Barcelona was its capital, and the list dates it 1640 to 1641. The area is now divided between Spain and France. The row gives no further detail on who declared it or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (Swedish protectorate, 1655 to 1657)
entries_new.recognition: Under Swedish protection, per the list
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes this Grand Duchy of Lithuania as a dominium directum protectorate of the Swedish Empire under King Charles X Gustav, in accordance with the Union of Kėdainiai. The list says it existed de jure, in law, from 1655 until 1657 and gives Kėdainiai as capital. The area is now in Lithuania, Belarus and Poland.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Grand Principality of Ruthenia
entries_new.challenge: Polish society (strong resistance, per the list)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Grand Principality of Ruthenia as a project of Ruthenia (Ukraine) as a member of the Polish-Lithuanian-Ruthenian Commonwealth, on the territory of the Kiev, Bracław and Chernihiv Voivodeships. Hetman Ivan Vyhovsky proposed it in September 1658. The first version of the Treaty of Hadiach approved it, but strong resistance in Polish society led to the idea being abandoned.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (1812)
entries_new.recognition: Created under French occupation, per the list
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes this as a Napoleonic attempt to restore the historical Grand Duchy of Lithuania after the Grande Armée occupied Vilnius on 28 June 1812. Established on 1 July 1812, the provisional government had seven committees and a president. It raised an army that cost 500,000 francs to create, and a native Lithuanian regiment that served in Napoleon's Imperial Guard.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Lithuanian Provisional Governing Commission
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states records the Lithuanian Provisional Governing Commission for 1812 to 1813, with Vilnius as its capital. The list says it merged with the Duchy of Warsaw to form the General Confederation of the Kingdom of Poland, which has its own row in the list.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: General Confederation of the Kingdom of Poland
entries_new.recognition: Puppet state of France, per the list
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the General Confederation of the Kingdom of Poland as a puppet state of France, meaning a state controlled by a foreign power, made from the reorganised Duchy of Warsaw during Napoleon's Russian campaign. Warsaw was its capital and the list dates it 1812 to 1813.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: State of Franche-Comté
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the State of Franche-Comté as a short-lived state that existed from January 27 to June 6, 1814. Its capital was Vesoul, in what is now France. The row gives no further detail on who ran it or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Poland (shadow government, 1831)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Kingdom of Poland of 1831 as a Polish shadow government established during the November Uprising, with Warsaw as capital. A shadow government is one that claims authority in competition with the ruling power. The row gives no further detail.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Government of Milan
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Provisional Government of Milan as an Italian revolutionary state established during the Revolutions of 1848. Milan was its capital. The row gives no further detail on its leaders or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: German Empire (1848 to 1849)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the German Empire of 1848 to 1849 as a short-lived proto-state, meaning a state in an early or incomplete form, with Frankfurt as capital. The list gives two views: in one it was a revolutionary new national state, and in another it was the reformed German Confederation.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Serbian Vojvodina
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes Serbian Vojvodina as a short-lived self-proclaimed Serb autonomous province within the Austrian Empire during the Revolutions of 1848. It existed until 1849, when it became a new official Austrian province, the Voivodeship of Serbia and Banat of Temeschwar. The list names Sremski Karlovci, Zemun, Zrenjanin and Timișoara as capitals.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Hungarian State (1849)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Hungarian State as a short-lived unrecognised state that existed for four months in the last phase of the Hungarian Revolution of 1848 to 1849. Buda was its capital. The area it covered is now in Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Austria, Slovakia and Ukraine.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Polish National Government (1863 to 1864)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Polish National Government of 1863 to 1864 as a Polish shadow government established during the January Uprising. A shadow government is one that claims authority in competition with the ruling power. The list names Warsaw, Vilnius and Kyiv as capitals.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Croatian People's Government
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Croatian People's Government as an attempt by the Croatian revolutionary Eugen Kvaternik to restore Croatian statehood after 769 years of foreign rule. The revolt lasted from 8 October 1871 to 11 October 1871. Its capital was Rakovica.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Catalan State (1873)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Catalan State of 1873 as a short-lived state in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands, with Barcelona as its capital. The row gives no further detail on who proclaimed it or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Tamrash
entries_new.story: The Republic of Tamrash was a self-governing administrative structure of the Pomaks living in the Tamrash region of the Rhodope Mountains. Wikipedia's list dates it 1878 to 1886 and gives Bulgaria as the country it is now part of. The list gives no capital.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Liubotyn Republic and Shuliavka Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Liubotyn Republic was proclaimed in December 1905 as an independent workers' state during the armed rising of workers and railwaymen in Liubotyn, and existed from December 26 to 30. The Shuliavka Republic was a worker-based quasi-government in Kyiv whose main task was self-defence. Its uprising lasted four days.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Zagłębie and Republic of Sławków
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Polish towns of Zagłębie Dąbrowskie and Sławków were taken over by revolutionaries during the Russian Revolution of 1905. Both republics existed in November and December 1905, each for about 10 to 12 days.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: General Government of Galicia and Bukovina
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the General Government of Galicia and Bukovina as a temporary Imperial Russian military administration of the eastern parts of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, captured from Austria-Hungary during the First World War. Lviv was the seat of administration, and the list dates it 1914 to 1917.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: General Government of Belgium
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the General Government of Belgium as a German Army occupation administration. It administered one of three separate occupation zones established in German-occupied Belgium during the First World War. Brussels was its capital, and the list dates it 1914 to 1918.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Government General of Warsaw
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Government General of Warsaw as an administrative civil district created by the German Empire in the First World War. It covered the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland. Warsaw was its capital, and the list dates it 1915 to 1918.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Military Government of Lublin
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Military Government of Lublin as a military administration of an area of the Russian Empire occupied by Austria-Hungary in the First World War. It ran under Governors-General, with its seat first at Kielce and, from October 1915, at Lublin. The list notes it existed from 1915 to 1917.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Land Council of Vidzeme
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Provisional Land Council of Vidzeme was created in the Governorate of Livonia on March 13, 1917, after the February Revolution in the Russian Empire. At first it supported Latvian land unity and self-determination, but by the second half of 1917 it came under increasing Bolshevik influence. On January 2, 1918 it ceased to exist, relinquishing its authority to the Bolshevik Iskolat.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Land Council of Courland
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Provisional Land Council of Courland was created on 27 April 1917 in Tartu as the representative organ of Courland Governorate. Courland had been under German military occupation since the summer of 1915, so the council sat in the Estonian city of Tartu. After the German offensive it was evacuated to the Russian city of Kazan in October 1917.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Crimean People's Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states records the Crimean People's Republic for 1917 to 1918, with Bakhchysarai as its capital. The row says only that it was defeated by the Red Army, and names Ukraine as the country the territory is now part of.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Land Council of Latgale
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Provisional Land Council of Latgale as a temporary governing body formed amid revolutionary upheaval to address urgent land reforms and local self-governance. The list gives Daugavpils as its capital with a question mark and dates the council 1917 to 1918. The territory is now part of Latvia.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.stopped_by: Union with the Kingdom of Romania

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.stopped_by: Ukrainian People's Republic with help from Germany and Austria
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Ukrainian People's Republic of Soviets as a Soviet Russia puppet state created through the efforts of local Bolsheviks and military support from Moscow and Petrograd. sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Executive Committee of the Soviet of Workers, Soldiers, and the Landless in Latvia
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes this Executive Committee as the governing body in the part of Latvia controlled by the pro-Communist Red Latvian Riflemen in 1917 to 1918. The list names Cēsis and Valka as its capitals.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: South-Eastern Union of Cossack Troops, Highlanders of the Caucasus, and Free Peoples of the Steppes
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the South-Eastern Union of Cossack Troops, Highlanders of the Caucasus, and Free Peoples of the Steppes as a short-lived anti-Bolshevik confederation. Yekaterinodar was its capital, and the list dates it 1917 to 1918. The territory is now in Ukraine and Russia.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Poland (client state, 1917 to 1918)
entries_new.stopped_by: Transformed into the Second Polish Republic in 1918
entries_new.recognition: Proclaimed by the German Empire and Austria-Hungary
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Kingdom of Poland was proclaimed by the German Empire and Austria-Hungary on 5 November 1916, on the Congress Poland territories held by the Central Powers, and became active on 14 January 1917. Between 7 October and 22 November 1918 it was transformed into the independent Second Polish Republic. The list calls it a client state, initially totally dependent on its sponsors.

entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states records the Union of Highlanders for 1917 to 1919, also known as the Mountainous Republic of the Northern Caucasus. Buynaksk was its capital, in present-day Russia. The row gives no further detail on its leaders or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Orenburg Cossack Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Orenburg Cossack Republic as a provisional government established by Cossacks in Orenburg. sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (1917 to 1922)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states includes the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic for 1917 to 1922, describing it as a revolutionary soviet state led by Vladimir Lenin during the Russian Civil War. sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Mainz Workers' and Soldiers' Council
entries_new.stopped_by: Arrival of French troops on 9 December 1918
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Mainz Workers' and Soldiers' Council as the effective government of Mainz, in present-day Germany, from 9 November until the arrival of French troops on 9 December 1918, during the German Revolution of 1918.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Supreme Administration of the Northern Region
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Supreme Administration of the Northern Region as an anti-Bolshevik left-wing Allied government that was part of the White movement during the Russian Civil War. The row notes that Allied warships sailed into the port of Arkhangelsk from the White Sea. The list dates it 1918.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs
entries_new.stopped_by: Merger with the Kingdom of Serbia, 1 December 1918
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs as a temporary state of the Austro-Hungarian South Slavs, declared on 29 October 1918. It merged with the Kingdom of Serbia on 1 December 1918, forming the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, which became Yugoslavia. Zagreb was its capital.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: First Republic of Pińczów
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the First Republic of Pińczów was the town of Pińczów and its surrounding area, captured at the end of 1918 for six weeks by the city's inhabitants. Jan Lisowski led them, after they disarmed the occupation troops without a fight. A separate row in the list covers a Second Republic of Pińczów in 1944.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic
entries_new.recognition: Soviet Russia
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic as lasting only three months during the Finnish Civil War, with Helsinki as its capital. The list notes that Soviet Russia recognized it. The territory is now in Finland and Russia.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Alsace-Lorraine Soviet Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states describes the Alsace-Lorraine Soviet Republic, also called the Republic of Alsace-Lorraine, as a soviet republic that existed in Alsace from 10 to 22 November 1918. Strasbourg is named as its capital, in present-day France.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Bunjevac People's Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Bunjevac People's Republic was proclaimed at Sombor in 1918, in alliance with the Banat Republic, to represent the interests of the Catholic Bunjevci. Sombor is now in Serbia. The row gives no further detail on its leaders or how it ended.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Chuvashia (state of 1918)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes Chuvashia in 1918 as the third indigenous Volga state declared during the Russian Civil War, after Idel-Ural and Bashkurdistan. The list gives no capital, and names Russia as the country the area is now part of.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Duchy of Courland and Semigallia (1918)

entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states records the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia of 1918 as a German client state, meaning a state dependent on a foreign sponsor. Riga is named as its capital, in present-day Latvia. The row gives no further detail.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Tarnobrzeg
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list says the Republic of Tarnobrzeg was proclaimed on November 6, 1918, in the Polish town of Tarnobrzeg. The list says it was disestablished in the spring of 1919 and dates it 1918 to 1919.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Crimean Regional Government
entries_new.recognition: German puppet state, per the list
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Crimean Regional Government as a short-lived government on the Crimean Peninsula and a German puppet state, meaning a state controlled by a foreign power. sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kars Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list of historical unrecognized states says the Kars Republic was declared by Muslims in Eastern Anatolia who sought unification with Azerbaijan. Kars was its capital, in present-day Turkey, and the list dates it 1918 to 1919.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Workers' and Peasants' Government of Ukraine
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Provisional Workers' and Peasants' Government of Ukraine as a provisional Soviet administration created to govern the areas of Ukraine occupied by Soviet Russia. Kharkiv was its capital, and the list dates it 1918 to 1919.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Komancza Republic
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Komancza Republic as an association of 30 pro-Ukrainian villages. It planned to merge with the West Ukrainian People's Republic but was suppressed by Poland during the Polish-Ukrainian War. Komańcza is named as its capital, and the list dates it 1918 to 1919.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of German-Austria
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Republic of German-Austria as a brief state declared after the collapse of Austria-Hungary. The Allies of the First World War opposed it, and it was succeeded by the First Austrian Republic. Vienna was the capital, and the territory is now in Austria and the Czech Republic.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic (1918 to 1919)
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes this Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic as a short-lived Soviet puppet state declared on 16 December 1918 by a provisional revolutionary government led by Vincas Mickevičius-Kapsukas. It ceased to exist on 27 February 1919, when it merged with the Socialist Soviet Republic of Byelorussia to form the Lithuanian-Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic (Litbel).

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Commune of the Working People of Estonia
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Commune of the Working People of Estonia as a communist government that administered the Bolshevik-occupied areas of Estonia during the Estonian War of Independence. Its capital was Narva, and the list dates it 1918 to 1919.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Aras
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's list describes the Republic of Aras as a state established during the Russian Civil War that lasted only several months. Its capital was Nakhchivan, in present-day Azerbaijan, and the list dates it 1918 to 1919.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
